Shruti Sharma was shifted to Apollo hospital by her parents for better treatment and at Apollo hospital she was found fit for statement at 4.00 p.m.

The SDM reached Apollo hospital and recorded statement (dying declaration) of Shruti Sharma, wherein she named her husband and inlaws for causing cruelty to her and for burning her by pouring kerosene oil.
On the basis of this statement, rukka was sent at about 5.20 p.m. and FIR was registered at PS Timar Pur.
The crime team inspected the spot of occurrence and exhibits were lifted from the spot by the police.

On 16.08.2006 Shruti Sharma succumbed to the injuries at Apollo hospital and thereafter the case was converted u/s 304B IPC.
The inquest proceedings were conducted by the SDM and investigating officer and postmortem on the dead body was got conducted.
On completion of investigation, the charge sheet was submitted against all the accused.
3. The case was committed to the court of sessions since the offence u/s 304B IPC is exclusively triable by the court of sessions.

4. On 09.07.2007, all the accused were charged for having committed offences punishable u/s 498 A IPC read with section 34 IPC and u/s 304B IPC read with section 34 IPC to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. During the trial, sisterinlaw accused Geeta expired and hence proceedings were abated against her vide order dated 27.03.2010.
6. Prosecution examined 29 witnesses in all to bring home the guilt of the accused.

50. Before dealing with the dying declaration, it is relevant to discuss the principles and rules governing the acceptability of the same.

The dying declaration is considered as a strong piece of evidence because the situation in which a person is on the death bed is so solemn and serene, that the grave position in which he is placed, is S.C.No. 57/10 Page 28 of 54 pages State Vs Anand Sharma etc. the reason in law to accept the veracity of his statement.
The Maxim is : '' A man will not meet his Maker with a lie in his mouth.''

A dying declaration made by the victim in a fit mental condition and on the verge of death has a special sanctity; at the solemn moment, a person is most unlikely to make an untrue statement, the shadow of impending death is itself the guarantee of the truth of his declaration as to the causes or circumstances leading to his death; a dying declaration is almost sacrosanct.

However, both accused have not led any strong evidence in their defence to establish their innocence.
The documents proved in defence do not raise any doubt about the prosecution case and do not favour the accused in any manner.
The accused have completely failed to rebut the presumption arising out u/s 113B Evidence Act.
71.
In the peculiar facts of the present case, even without having such S.C.No. 57/10 Page 46 of 54 pages State Vs Anand Sharma etc. presumption, the accused were required to offer reasonable explanation as to the incident and they could not get away by maintaining silence as the incident has taken place inside the bedroom in secrecy.
In this case, the accused persons have not furnished any explanation about the incident throughout the trial.
They have exhibited ignorance at every stage which is unnatural and unconvincing.
74. Significantly, the deceased in her dying declaration has excluded Om Prakash for being involved in causing cruelty to her or in causing burn injuries to her.
The deceased specifically named her husband, motherinlaw and sisterinlaw in her statement and the same leads to clear inference that deceased did not doubt her fatherinlaw to have been involved in the incident.
The conduct of Om Prakash is depicted from the testimony of parents and brother of deceased, and same is mitigating in nature rather than incriminating.
No specific and consistent allegations are leveled against him about cruelty towards the deceased.
The deceased too exonerated Om Prakash completely in her dying declaration by not attributing anything incriminating against him.
Dowry is customary extortion that tends to disgrace the sacred institution of marriage and despite all the economic and political progress, the evil of dowry is aggressively prevalent in the society.
It has not shown any decrease despite existence of stringent provisions on the statute book.
Taking one's life for dowry is so heinous and grave that leniency has no place to stand with it.
